Subject: Clarify: default auto-deletion boundaries for requests & artifacts

Hi team,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — we covered model routing but I still need a tightened answer for procurement/security: what exactly does Redwood remove automatically by default and when? In particular we need clarity on three items: 1) raw request payloads (user prompts + metadata), 2) model outputs (final completion and any streamed fragments), and 3) ephemeral artifacts like KV cache / streaming buffers.

BrightBank's compliance folks want concrete retention buckets and a short description of deletion triggers (customer-initiated purge vs automatic TTL vs legal hold). We also need to confirm whether anything is copied to a control plane log outside the customer VPC and whether deletion evidence can be produced for the audit.

Can you provide a concise bullet list and point to any published runbooks or a proof-of-deletion artifact we can include in our security package? We are targeting a go/no-go next week, so a quick turnaround would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Lydia

Hi Lydia —

Appreciate the clear ask. Below is a concise summary that you can drop into your package; I followed up with Kimberley for the exact runbook pointers and proof steps and she attached the operational playbook. High-level:

- Default retention for request payloads (user text + basic request metadata): 60 days. These live in the customer-scoped request log by default and are removed automatically at TTL unless the account has an active retention override or legal hold.

- Final model outputs (finalized completions): retained for 90 days by default. This includes final outputs persisted to the artifact store. Streaming fragments (intermediate tokens sent via streaming) are transient by default and kept only long enough to reconstruct session state (typically < 1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by the customer or captured by error logs during troubleshooting.

- KV cache and ephemeral serving buffers: considered ephemeral — not retained beyond the serving session. By default these are flushed on session termination; snapshots are only taken for debugging with customer consent and when collection is enabled in Dedicated/Private deployments.

- Control plane logs & audit traces: minimal routing and billing metadata are kept separately for 365 days for operational and billing reconciliation. Sensitive user content is not copied to long-term control-plane traces by default.

- Deletion triggers: automatic TTL expiry (above buckets), customer-initiated purge via API (on-demand remove), and account-level wipe for contract termination. For legal holds we freeze the retention pipeline and follow the preservation runbook.

Attached: retention_runbook_v2.pdf (operational steps) and a short checklist for production POC evidence. Kimberley will enumerate the proof-of-deletion artifacts we can provide for your audit.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the runbook and show the deletion logs.

Best,

Hi Lydia — adding the operational specifics you asked for. I kept it short and evidence-focused.

1) Request payloads (default 60d)
   - Storage: persisted in customer-scoped request buckets (hosted: encrypted, multiregion aware; private: stays in customer VPC).
   - Deletion evidence: our system writes a tombstone record when TTL expires and an audit log entry with deletion-job id. We can export the deletion-job id and timestamp for a given data key on request (CSV).

2) Final outputs (default 90d)
   - Storage: artifact store with retention metadata. When a deletion is executed we mark the artifact as expunged and run background shredding (object unlink + overwrite window). Certificate: we can provide a signed manifest of deleted object ids for the time range requested.

3) Streaming fragments & KV cache
   - Streaming fragments: buffered in-memory/short-lived buffer; default purge is immediate after session consolidation (under 1 hour). We do not index streaming fragments into long-term logs unless capture is enabled.
   - KV cache: kept in volatile GPU memory with optional periodic snapshots for debugging only. Snapshots require explicit enablement and are stored under a different TTL (customer-controlled).

4) Control-plane & billing traces
   - Non-sensitive routing/billing traces retained up to 365d. Full content payloads are not mirrored there by default.

5) Proof-of-deletion options we can deliver
   - deletion-job CSV exports, signed deletion manifests, and where applicable a short redacted sample showing object id -> deletion timestamp.
   - For EU pilots we provide residency stamp + manifest signed with our KMS key.

Attachments: retention_runbook_v2.pdf (step-by-step), deletion_playbook_steps.txt (commands and API endpoints).

Let me know which artifact you need first and we’ll produce a sample manifest for your auditors.

Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
